items.name: Eigendrum
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Eigendrum - Draw any shape and hear what it sounds like as a drum
items.summary: A browser drum visualizer that turns drawn shapes into resonant sounds.
items.why_included: Two commenters directly praised the interactive visualizer as brilliant and revealing.
items.evidence: Commenters called Eigendrum brilliant and a great visualizer tool, with one saying it revealed a connection to cymatics.

items.name: Silent Shark
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Silent Shark – tactical map-based WWII submarine sim
items.summary: A tactical map-based World War II submarine simulation game with native Linux support.
items.why_included: A purchaser gave unusually concrete first-hand praise for both the game and tutorial.
items.evidence: A buyer said Silent Shark was really fun and that its tutorial was great after trying the Linux version.

evidence_sources.author: marvinblum
evidence_sources.excerpt: I bought it a few days ago. Thank you for including native Linux support <3 So far, it's really fun and the tutorial is great!

items.name: Racket
items.summary: A language-oriented programming language with a featureful runtime and standard library.
items.why_included: A decade-long maintainer described substantial real-world use and concrete strengths.
items.evidence: A long-time Racket user praised its runtime, standard library, threading, FFI, and macro design.

evidence_sources.author: pavpanchekha
evidence_sources.excerpt: Racket is great! The runtime is reasonably fast, and the standard library is exceptionally featureful

items.name: Fugashi
items.summary: A Python wrapper for MeCab, a Japanese-language tokenizer.
items.why_included: The package was singled out within a strongly positive first-hand account of Japanese NLP work.
items.evidence: A language-learning developer said Paul McCann's Japanese NLP work had really helped their projects and identified Fugashi as his MeCab wrapper.

evidence_sources.author: joshdavham
evidence_sources.excerpt: He’s done awesome work in the Japanese NLP space over the last decade which has really helped me in my language learning projects. He maintains a mecab (Japanese tokenizer) wrapper for Python

items.name: HitchStory
items.source_story_title: Yadda 3.0.0: BDD in the Age of AI Agents
items.summary: A typed YAML story framework for executable integration-test specifications.
items.why_included: A practitioner preferred it over Cucumber because its YAML stories are terse and typed.
items.evidence: A commenter described using HitchStory for YAML-based stories and valued its terse, typed format.

evidence_sources.author: MoreQARespect
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used hitchstory (YAML based stories) for doing this coz it's terse and typed.
